paper: Jayaraman, Wu & Jiang (2020), Should I Stay or Should I Grow? Using Voluntary Disclosure to Elicit Market Feedback, RFS 33(8), 3854-3888
annotator: Member D, written independently from the published paper text only; page numbers are PDF pages of the published RFS version.
rule: Values record what the paper states. If the paper does not state a field, the value is null. Notes cite the paper only.

sample_filters: firms making annual capex forecasts covered by IBES, matched to Compustat using the IBES link file (initial sample of 40,785 forecasts, 2002-2016)
matched with CRSP to obtain the short-window market reaction on the issuance date (reduces the sample to 36,900 forecasts)
delete forecasts made concurrently with an earnings forecast (17,473 forecasts deleted)
delete forecasts made in 2016 because actual capital expenditure data as of the end of the year are needed (1,850 forecasts deleted)
fields.dependent_var: CAPEX_ADJ: percentage deviation of actual capex from forecasted capex scaled by the latter; for range forecasts, the difference between annual capex and the endpoints of the range (upper end for upward, lower end for downward adjustments), scaled by the forecast
key_independent_vars: CAR: cumulative abnormal return (firm return minus S&P 500 index return) over the 5 days [-2, 2] surrounding the forecast date, standardized to have a zero mean and unit standard deviation
controls: SIZE: log of market value of equity
LAG_CAPX: most recent year's annual capex scaled by start of year market value (Table 2 note)
SURP: earnings surprise for the most recent quarter, the quarter's EPS minus that of the same quarter of the previous year
EA_DUM: indicator for capex forecasts made concurrently with earnings announcements
fields.fixed_effects: none in Models 1 and 2; year-quarter fixed effects in Model 3; firm and year-quarter fixed effects in Models 4 to 8
fields.standard_errors: robust standard errors clustered by firm in Models 1 to 4 and by industry in Models 5 to 8
fields.subsamples: columns add specification elements progressively: Model 1 univariate; Model 2 adds SIZE; Model 3 adds year-quarter fixed effects; Model 4 adds firm fixed effects; Model 5 switches clustering to industry; Model 6 falsification test adding SF_CAR (market reaction to sales forecasts) on the 3,456-forecast subsample with a matching sales forecast; Model 7 falsification tests adding MKTRET (S&P 500 return on the forecast date) and CAR_PRE (pseudo 5-day market reaction around a non-forecast day 2 weeks prior); Model 8 adds LAG_CAPX, SURP and EA_DUM
fields.sample_size: 17,577 in Models 1 to 5 and 7; 3,456 in Model 6; 17,505 in Model 8

notes.sample_period: Initial sample covers 2002-2016 (p.8); 2016 forecasts are deleted, so the final period is 2003-2015 (p.8).
notes.data_sources: Section 1.2 (p.8) also lists Easley et al.'s PIN data from Brown et al. (2004), but Table 2 uses no PIN-based variable; the spread split appears in Table 3.
notes.sample_filters: Filters on p.8; final sample 17,577 forecasts by 1,790 unique firms. 'Concurrent with an earnings forecast' is not defined further; forecasts concurrent with quarterly earnings announcements are retained (footnote 15, p.8).
notes.unit_of_observation: 'Our unit of observation in most tables is a firm-quarter' (p.8).
notes.dependent_var: Definition in Section 1.2 (p.8) and the Table 1 note (p.9); range-forecast handling on p.10 (Section 2.1 area).
notes.key_independent_vars: CAR is standardized to have a zero mean and unit standard deviation (p.10 text; Table 2 note, p.11). SF_CAR, MKTRET and CAR_PRE enter only as falsification variables in Models 6-7 and are described under subsamples.
notes.controls: Table 2 note (p.11) defines LAG_CAPX as 'the most recent year's annual capex scaled by start of year market value' (also 'scaled by market value' on p.12), while the Table 1 note (p.9) reports LAG_CAPX 'in US$ millions' — the descriptive-statistics variable and the regression control differ in scaling.
notes.fixed_effects: Table 2 note (p.11): Model 3 includes year-quarter fixed effects, Models 4 to 8 firm and year-quarter fixed effects.
notes.standard_errors: Industry clustering is the main specification (p.10); the firm-to-industry switch between Models 4 and 5 is stated in the Table 2 note (p.11). The industry classification is not defined anywhere in the paper.
notes.model: The paper says 'we estimate the following regression' (p.10); OLS is not named explicitly.
notes.subsamples: Model descriptions on pp.11-12; the Model 6 subsample of 3,456 forecasts with a corresponding sales forecast is footnote 22 (p.12); the median sales forecast is 86 days away from the capex forecast.
notes.winsorization: No statement about winsorizing, trimming or outliers anywhere in the paper.
notes.sample_size: Obs. row of Table 2 (p.11); the drop from 17,577 to 17,505 in Model 8 is not explained in the text.
